claims.text: DFT calculations can predict low-temperature sintering pathways for ceramic or powder materials.
Using DFT-predicted pathways can reduce the sintering temperature.
The relevant material begins in an unsintered or green state.
DFT calculations modify the material's potential-energy landscape.
Modification of the potential-energy landscape lowers the energy barrier for sintering.
Lowering the sintering energy barrier reduces the required sintering temperature.
The proposed intervention will reduce the sintering temperature by at least 100°C relative to conventional sintering.
The proposed pathway applies at sintering temperatures below 800°C.
The exchange-correlation functional can affect the accuracy of DFT predictions of low-temperature sintering pathways.
The level of theory can affect the accuracy of DFT predictions of low-temperature sintering pathways.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes DFT as a predictive method for identifying pathways, whereas the intervention describes the calculations themselves as physically modifying the material's potential-energy landscape. A calculation can characterize or guide a material modification, but the actual modifying treatment is not specified.
